sections.title: Recent Advances and Future Directions
sections.text:
TLDR; Recent advances in hyperbolic machine learning have focused on developing more sophisticated architectures and applications, particularly in foundation models and multimodal learning. Future directions point toward more efficient implementations, better theoretical frameworks, and expanded applications across domains. (7 sources)

The field of hyperbolic machine learning has seen significant recent developments, particularly in the development of foundation models and more sophisticated architectures. Notable advances include the creation of hyperbolic transformers with linear attention mechanisms, hyperbolic vision-language models, and specialized fine-tuning methods for large language models  [274859756 | He et al. | 2024 | Citations: 5].

A key area of recent progress has been in developing fully hyperbolic architectures that operate entirely within hyperbolic space, eliminating the need for frequent conversions to tangent space  [277628124 | Cheng et al. | 2025 | Citations: 1]. This advancement has led to more efficient implementations and better utilization of hyperbolic geometry's properties.

The field has also made significant strides in addressing specific technical challenges. Recent work has focused on improving model efficiency through techniques like hyperbolic diffusion geometry and developing more stable implementations of neural operations in hyperbolic space  [277501898 | Yuan et al. | 2025 | Citations: 2].

Looking toward the future, researchers are exploring several promising directions. These include the development of hyperbolic foundation models that can handle increasingly complex tasks, with particular emphasis on visual representation learning and multimodal applications  [277781202 | He et al. | 2025 | Citations: 2]. The field is also moving toward more sophisticated approaches for machine unlearning and knowledge preservation in hyperbolic spaces  [277113146 | Vidal et al. | 2025 | Citations: 1].

The integration of reinforcement learning with hyperbolic geometry represents another frontier, particularly for applications involving hierarchical decision-making processes [275471607 | Ja'cimovi'c | 2025 | Citations: 1]. This direction shows promise for addressing complex sequential decision problems where hierarchical structure plays a crucial role.

A notable trend is the development of more specialized algorithms for hyperbolic spaces, including adaptations of traditional machine learning methods like expectation-maximization and variational inference [275471607 | Ja'cimovi'c | 2025 | Citations: 1]. These developments are laying the groundwork for more sophisticated deep learning pipelines that can fully leverage the unique properties of hyperbolic geometry.

citations.title: [274859756 | He et al. | 2024 | Citations: 5]
snippets: Hyperbolic spaces have garnered extensive attention in recent years for representation learning and deep learning [26,30,47]. A defining geometric characteristic of hyperbolic spaces is their negative curvature, which results in an exponential growth of volume with distance from the origin. This property closely mirrors the structure of tree-like data, where the number of child nodes increases exponentially [19]. Consequently, hyperbolic representation learning provides a strong geometric prior for hierarchical structures, tree-like data, and power-law distributed information. Significant advancements have been achieved in various domains such as Word-Net [28,29], graphs [3, 24, 45, 50, 53], social networks [46,49], and recommendation systems [6,37,44,48] utilizing hyperbolic representations. Moreover, hyperbolic deep learning has demonstrated impressive performance in image-related tasks, including image embedding [10,15,18] and segmentation [1,4,42], offering new insights into deep learning paradigms, such as the interpretation of norms as reflections of uncertainty. Within the neural network domain, HNN [12] presented the pioneering form of hyperbolic neural networks, defining fundamental hyperbolic transformations, classifiers, and hyperbolic multiclass logistic regression (MLR). HNN++ [35] further reduced the parameter count of hyperbolic MLR and made advancements in fully connected layers, the splitting and concatenation of coordinates, convolutional layers, and attention mechanisms within hyperbolic space. Recent studies, such as HyboNet [5] and Hypformer [45] propose frameworks that construct neural networks entirely within hyperbolic space, contrasting with existing models that partially operate in Euclidean tangent spaces Several works have explored the adaptation of residual connections to hyperbolic spaces.

citations.title: [275471607 | Ja'cimovi'c | 2025 | Citations: 1]
snippets: Recent advances in hyperbolic representations of data open exciting perspectives and horizons for the near future. Encouraging results have been reported in natural language processing (NLP) [4,(Nickel et al., 2018)[6], computer vision (Mettes et al., 2023)(Khrulkov et al., 2019), molecular interactions (Poleksic, 2023)(Corso et al., 2021), recommender systems [11,(Li et al., 2021), knowledge graphs [13] and brain research (Baker et al., 2023)(Allard et al., 2018)[16]. In addition, some researchers devised a general hyperbolic-geometric approach to reinforcement learning (RL), due to the hierarchical nature of Markov decision processes [17] One can build upon the concepts and methods presented here in order to design various algorithms in hyperbolic spaces, including expectation-maximization algorithm, Bayesian filtering, variational inference, normalizing flows, etc. Implementation of these algorithms would create a sufficient machinery for deep learning pipelines in hyperbolic spaces.

citations.title: [277113146 | Vidal et al. | 2025 | Citations: 1]
snippets: This paper investigates machine unlearning in hyperbolic contrastive learning by adapting Alignment Calibration to MERU, a model that embeds images and text in hyperbolic space to better capture semantic hierarchies Our approach introduces hyperbolic-specific components including entailment calibration and norm regularization that leverage the unique properties of hyperbolic space This work bridges two important research areas: geometric representation learning and machine unlearning.

citations.title: [277501898 | Yuan et al. | 2025 | Citations: 2]
snippets: Currently, Non-Euclidean representation learning, particularly hyperbolic representation learning, plays a crucial role in recommender systems (RSs) (Sun et al., 2021)(Tran et al., 2018)[69]. HyperML (Tran et al., 2018) investigates metric learning in hyperbolic space and its connection to collaborative filtering. Similarly, HGCF (Sun et al., 2021) proposes a hyperbolic GCN model for CF. In order to address the power-law distribution in recommender systems, HICF (Yang et al., 2022) focuses on enhancing the attention towards tail items in hyperbolic spaces, incorporating geometric awareness into the pull and push process. Interestingly, GDCF [69] aims to capture intent factors across geometric spaces by learning geometric disentangled representations associated with user intentions and different geometries. On the other hand, paper (Xu et al., 2019) highlights that the naive inner product used in the factorization machine model (Rendle, 2010) may not adequately capture spurious or implicit feature interactions. Collaborative metric learning (Hsieh et al., 2017) proposes that learning the distance instead of relying on the inner product provides benefits in capturing detailed embedding spaces that encompass item-user interactions, item-item relationships, and user-user distances simultaneously. Consequently, the triangle inequality emerges as a more favorable alternative to the inner product. Paper (Lin et al., 2023) is the first to introduce the use of hyperbolic diffusion geometry to reveal hierarchical structures. Similarly, HypDiff (Fu et al., 2024) leverages hyperbolic diffusion for graph generation.

citations.title: [277628124 | Cheng et al. | 2025 | Citations: 1]
snippets: The geometric properties of hyperbolic space make hyperbolic neural networks highly effective for modeling data with hierarchical structures. In recommender systems, this ability to capture the inherent hierarchical relationships in user-item interactions has been increasingly recognized. Early efforts in this field focus on adapting techniques from Euclidean space. For example, HyperML [29] and HME [5] introduce metric learning into hyperbolic space recommender systems. HVAE [19] designs a variational autoencoder model on hyperbolic space. HGCF [28] proposes a Hyperbolic Graph Convolution Network (HGCN). These studies demonstrate the advantages of hyperbolic space through notable performance. Consequently, recent research has explored more efficient ways to leverage hyperbolic space. For instance, HRCF [38] proposes a hyperbolic geometric aware regularizer loss, and HICF [37] enhances margin ranking loss with adaptive margins. However, due to the challenges in formalizing neural operations within hyperbolic space, earlier methods often map vectors to Euclidean space for computation, then back to hyperbolic space, resulting in suboptimal utilization of the hyperbolic space. To address this limitation, LGCF [32], GGCF [35], and HGCH [40] respectively propose fully HGCN on Klein, Hyperboloid, and Poincaré hyperbolic spaces, which perform computation entirely within hyperbolic space.

citations.title: [277781202 | He et al. | 2025 | Citations: 2]
snippets: Recent studies have made significant progress toward building hyperbolic foundation models. HNN [25] and HNN++ [51] developed many basic operations, such as hyperbolic linear and convolutional layers, and multinomial logistic regression (MLR). HGCN [6] and HGNN [39] were then among the first to adapt graph neural networks (GNNs) to hyperbolic spaces. More recently, HyboNet [10] proposed a framework of hyperbolic neural networks that does not depend on the Euclidean tangent spaces; Poincaré ResNet [54] and HCNN [4] developed essential components for hyperbolic computer vision models; Hypformer (Yang et al., 2024) developed numerous essential hyperbolic modules to propose an efficient hyperbolic Transformer model that operates directly on the manifold; LResNet (He et al., 2024) proposed an efficient and stable Lorentzian residual connection method, and HypLoRA extended the LoRA fine-tuning methods to Lorentz space (Yang et al., 2024). Several works have also developed essential module such as hyperbolic entailment cone and contrastive loss for contrastive learning (Desai et al., 2023)(Pal et al., 2024) Recent studies have made significant advances to the development of hyperbolic foundation models, including Transformers [10,(Gülçehre et al., 2018)[51] with hyperbolic attention mechanisms, hyperbolic Transformers with linear attention (Yang et al., 2024), hyperbolic vision Transformers (Fein-Ashley et al., 2024), hyperbolic pretrained large language models (Chen et al., 2024), hyperbolic fine-tuning methods for LLMs (Yang et al., 2024), and hyperbolic vision-language models (Desai et al., 2023)(Pal et al., 2024) many recent works have shown that embedding data in hyperbolic manifolds have the potential to improve expressiveness and efficiency in representation learning for a wide range of applications, with significant advancements in domains such as languages [7,20,42,43], graphs [6,39,62,66,68,70], social networks [63,67], recommendation systems [12,52,61,65], image embedding [23,29,34], and segmentation [2,8]57].
